Categories.value: Images with intentional borders|Tiretta Bazaar|Artworks without Wikidata item|PD-old-100-expired|PD-Art (PD-old-100-expired)|Kolkata in the 1850s|CC-PD-Mark|Images uploaded by Broichmore|Indian spices for English Tables, or, A rare relish of fun from the Far East (1860)

Artist.value: George Francklin Atkinson

ImageDescription.value:
Plate 4.

After breakfast he shows himself in the China Bazaar, and is gratified at the genial reception he meets with which however is to be attributed to a praiseworthy anxiety on the part of the shopkeepers to reach the pockets of so promising a customer.

He selects a cap from a variety of specimens.

Plate from Captain George Francklin Atkinson's, Indian spices for English Tables, or, A rare relish of fun from the Far East. Being, the adventures of "our special correspondent" in India, illustrated in a series of one hundred and twenty sketches, and exhibiting, in all its phases, the peculiarity of life in that country, London: Day & Son, Ltd., 1860.
